**Phase 2 (post-training) contributes the larger gain: about +35–50% in offline MRR compared with a freshly trained Phase-1 model.** (p. 7, Table 1 and Section 5.3)

- **Phase 2:** The 35–50% gain is measured on the Phase-1 training cutoff date, when the Phase-1 model is at its freshest. The paper credits task-specific adaptation, including domain-specific data, rewards and verbalizations. (p. 7)
- **Gain grows over time:** About two weeks later, Phase 2's improvement rises to roughly 80%. The authors attribute this partly to the Phase-1 backbone going stale, since it is updated less often, as content popularity and member interests shift. (p. 7)
- **Phase 1:** Using the Phase-1 foundation model as the base improves offline ranking metrics by about 10–20% compared with an off-the-shelf open-source LLM. (p. 7, Table 1 and Section 5.3)

The two gains are measured against different baselines. Phase 1 is compared with an open-source model, and Phase 2 is compared with a freshly trained Phase-1 model. So "larger" here means the reported percentage is larger. It is not a comparison against a single shared baseline. (p. 7, Table 1)
